newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria puts in circulation 50,000-lev note May 8.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria puts in circulation 50,000-lev note May 8.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) said on Friday it would put into circulation a 50,000-lev note next week, the largest denomination to go in use so far.
"A 50,000 lev note will go in circulation on May 8," the BNB said in a statement.
Soaring inflation measured at 2,041 percent year on year in March has made larger denominations necessary to ease large payments and to cut the cost of maintaining the volume of money in circulation.
The new note will be worth around $33.50 under the current lev/dollar exchange rate. @
The largest denomination in use so far has been a 10,000-lev note, which was put into circulation on December 9, 1996.
Levs in circulation rose to 338.4 billion levs on April 18 from 311 billion levs a week earlier and 127 billion levs at end-1996, preliminary central bank figures showed.
Monthly inflation for March was 12.3 percent and cumulative inflation for the first quarter was 452.3 percent. Annual inflation for 1996 was 311 percent.
Monthly inflation rate for April was projected below March's level, a National Statistics Institute official said. @
Under a memorandum of economic policies agreed with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) annual inflation for this year was projected at 769 percent and at 14 percent for next year.

The 50,000-lev note depicts the brothers Cyril and Methodius who created the Cyrilic alphabet in the 9th century. Initially the notes will be printed in Germany but printing will be transferred to Bulgaria in the second half of the year.
Last week the government approved the design of a 20,000-lev note but declined to say when it was expected to be put into circulation. @

A 100,000 lev-note, the largest denomination planned so far, was also approved by the government last month. It was expected to be put into circulation in the autumn. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
